chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about what is brought out from the sea, such as pearls, ruby, and chrysolite, and about the mines of gold and silver—what is due regarding them?
He عليه السلام said: When its value reaches one dīnār, then khums is due on it.

key_terms.الزَّبَرْجَدِ: chrysolite or a precious green gemstone
key_terms.الْبَحْرِ: the sea, from which valuables are extracted
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth due as a prescribed religious levy
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a dīnār, the threshold value mentioned for obligation
key_terms.مَعَادِنِ: mines or mineral sources in the earth

ai.seo_question: When does khums become obligatory on pearls, gemstones, and mined gold or silver in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning khums on certain extracted valuables, including sea produce such as pearls and precious stones, as well as mined gold and silver. It states that when the value reaches one dīnār, khums becomes due.
